faqPage.title: Everything you need to know about AIOS
faqPage.subtitle: Answers about Founder Beta, Harmony, Julius, the AI workforce, marketplace, templates, integrations, security, and access.

items.a: AIOS is an autonomous operating platform for building and running AI-assisted companies. Harmony is the AI Chief of Staff, Julius is the organizational brain, and the AI workforce, marketplace, templates, and integrations operate together under human approval.

items.q: How is AIOS different from other AI tools?
items.a: Most AI tools assist: they draft, summarize, or answer. AIOS coordinates an operating system: company context, memory, workforce routing, approvals, marketplace capabilities, and governed execution.
AIOS Founder Beta is for founders and early operators who want to validate an AI-assisted operating model before a broader public beta.

items.q: Do I need to be technical to use it?
items.a: No. You describe goals in plain language, review the workspace, and approve meaningful actions. AIOS handles routing and coordination behind the scenes.

items.q: What are the core product areas?
items.a: The public launch focuses on Harmony, Julius, Company Builder, Templates, Marketplace, AI Workforce, Integrations, Settings, and the Founder Command Center.

items.q: Can I start from a template?
items.a: Yes. Company Templates are designed to give you a starting operating model: departments, objectives, workforce activation, and connector planning.

items.q: What is the Founder Command Center?
items.a: A single screen for founders to steer the operation: companies, objectives, approvals, activity, recommendations, workforce status, and launch signals.
No. AIOS is designed to amplify operators and teams by routing routine work, preserving context, and keeping judgment-heavy decisions with humans.

items.q: What can the AI workforce actually do?
items.a: The workforce can help route work, prepare recommendations, coordinate content and communications, monitor operations, preserve knowledge, and execute approved low-risk tasks depending on configuration.
Always. AIOS is built around approvals, guardrails, autonomy levels, and audit trails. You decide what can run automatically and what must wait for review.
High-risk autonomy is not assumed. Founder Beta should begin with controlled settings, approvals, and explicit verification before expanding automation.
You do. Data ownership is a core AIOS principle. Export, deletion, and retention practices should be verified for the account type before broader public rollout.

AIOS uses owner-scoped data access patterns, Supabase RLS, token-at-rest encryption support, admin boundaries, CSP, and approval-oriented workflows. Production settings still need Founder verification.

items.q: Can I see what the AI helpers did?
items.a: Yes. Every meaningful action is logged in a reviewable audit trail, so nothing happens as a black box.
Create an account or request Founder Beta access. AIOS is currently targeted at controlled Founder Beta onboarding rather than open public self-serve launch.
Priority onboarding, direct feedback loops, and influence over the product roadmap while the operating model is validated.

items.q: Can I buy AIOS from the public pricing page?
items.a: No. Public checkout, Stripe, payments, and entitlements are inactive. Pricing is shown for planning and Founder Beta positioning only.

autonomy.title: Autonomy
autonomy.subtitle: Bounded autonomy controls and audit. Everything stays advisory until you enable it.
autonomy.runPassHint: Evaluate proposed work against policy, record decisions, and auto-complete only eligible safe items.
autonomy.applyTierHint: Set Tier 1/2/3 defaults per agent and open the safe categories. Does not enable the global switch.

help.mode: Controls whether autonomy can run at all. The stricter of global mode and per-agent mode always wins.

modes.off: No autonomous execution. Work can still be proposed, but execution is denied or routed to approval.
modes.advisory: Harmony and agents can recommend work, but founder approval is required before execution.
modes.bounded: Eligible low/medium-risk work can execute only inside category, risk, and quota limits.

help.autoThreshold: Highest risk level the global policy may auto-execute. None means no automatic execution.
help.agentThreshold: Optional per-agent override. Inherit uses the global threshold; the most restrictive threshold wins.
help.maxActionsPerHour: Maximum autonomous actions allowed per hour across the global policy. 0 disables hourly autonomous execution.
help.maxDelegationDepth: Maximum nested agent handoffs allowed during an autonomous pass. 0 disables delegation chaining.
help.notifyOnMedium: When enabled, medium-risk auto-executions are recorded as auto plus notified.
help.killSwitch: Stops all autonomy immediately regardless of mode, category, risk, or quota.
help.lockdown: Freezes autonomous execution for founder review while keeping audit visibility.
help.daily: Daily auto-action budget for this agent. It counts auto-executed and auto plus notified decisions since UTC midnight. 0 disables auto-execution for the agent.
help.monthly: Monthly auto-action budget for this agent. It counts auto-executed and auto plus notified decisions since the first day of the UTC month. 0 disables auto-execution for the agent.
help.approvalOnly: Restricted categories are hard-coded to require founder approval and cannot be opened for autonomy.
help.autoAllowed: Allows this non-restricted category to be considered for bounded auto-execution.
help.requiresApproval: Forces approval for this category even when the category is otherwise auto-allowed.
help.maxRisk: Highest risk this category may auto-execute. Low is routine only; Medium can execute when global and agent thresholds also allow it.

content.publishingNote: Communications content can progress autonomously per policy. Publishing always requires founder approval.
